profile.headline: Software Engineer at PURVIS Systems
profile.summary: Software Engineer for PURVIS Systems, on-site at the Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) in Newport, Rhode Island.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Solved and delivered in a timely manner software fixes for problems reported by customers. Took part of proactive teams that analyzed and provided solutions to data and time sensitive customer’s problems. Worked in the academic field in various ventures. Set up and maintained a high performance cluster in order to perform ocean modeling simulations. Developed a Grid web portal that ran web services over distributed resources to perform signal processing operators, and taught diverse programming and software tools courses to undergrad college students. Have gained knowledge and team collaboration strategies along this journey from many experts and great team players.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Performed as Sr Software Engineering of a scrum development team helping to develop the product’s new feature based on Java, using GitHub, Maven and Eclipse.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Performed as scrum master and software engineer of a scrum development team that delivers the new product features of our database management system as well as helping to provide to our customers the solutions to their required improvements and fixes for the product. Helped in the modernization process of CA IDMS by helping to develop the new Web services feature and technical documentation. Have helped to deliver the status and futures of the new feature to customers by presenting at the product technical conferences. CA IDMS database management system is the Mainframe product family which I worked with using IBM Assembler and COBOL languages.

positions.title: IT Specialist
positions.description:
Worked as IT Specialist at the Computational Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Group, running numerical models of Narragansett Bay circulation on a new supercomputer cluster, located at the Graduate School of Oceanography (URI-GSO), Narragansett Bay Campus, RI. 
Performed general cluster and networking maintenance, cluster setting, bash programming and management for the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) and Underworld Project.

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description:
SUAGM at Carolina, Yauco and Santa Isabel campusses.
Instructed undergraduate college students in software, design and programming skills. 
Taught courses: Logic Programming, Internet and MS-Office Integration, Introduction to Databases, HTML Web Design, Introduction to Computer and Software, Microsoft Access and Excel. Designed the curriculum oriented to practical lab classes thought as small projects in order to seed and improve the student’s skills.Participated in a project funded by the Department of Labor and Human Resources of Puerto Rico teaching to adult and displaced workers the fundamental of QuickBooks, Access, Publisher and FrontPage and designed the curriculum based on audience and needs of industries. Used ability to break down information easily and convey theory to students.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description: Research project funded by the NSA (National Science Foundation): “A Grid Portal for Environmental Monitoring Applications”. Developed a grid portal user interface to access environmental applications of signal processing operators. Implemented the operators as a set of distributed Grid (Web) services. Used GridSphere portal framework to implement the user interface, Globus Toolkit to provide the grid computing support and Java Portlet Specification standard as the interface with the grid portal and the grid services consumption side.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Helped with the software customization for the course management system -MOODLE- in order to meet the institution's requirements.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Served as teaching assistant and grader for the Introduction to Computer Technologies course. Supervised undergraduate college students.

volunteerExperiences.description: Have been a networking professional volunteer in three 6 Degrees Networking Professional events. Networking professional meets and mingles with 8th grade students for a night of hand shaking, small talking, and business card swapping. Networking Professionals answer student questions about their own professional journeys and give advice to the next generation of leaders and innovators. Additionally, have the opportunity to do some personal networking with other service-oriented and like-minded community members.

volunteerExperiences.companyName: Rhode Island Students of the Future
volunteerExperiences.description:
Have been a volunteer staff for the past three Robot Block Party events, sponsored by the
Rhode Island School of the Future and the Humanity Based Robotics Initiative at Brown University in Rhode Island. The Robot Block Party brings together robotics innovators from industry, universities, community organizations and K-12 schools.
